tagline: Logging roads through the rainforest, from totem park to totem park.
intro: The ferry from Ketchikan takes three hours to cross to Hollis, a mining town from 1900 to about 1915, later a logging camp, now a hundred people and a ferry landing. From there mostly paved roads run out through the Tongass rainforest to the island's small towns. The island holds the most extensive road system in the whole forest, built for the logging companies and now open to everyone else.
Not everyone wanted in. In 1974 Point Baker and Port Protection chose not to be connected.

moments.title: Hydaburg
moments.text: Three Haida villages on Cordova Bay came together here in 1911, picking the spot for its reliable water, and the town keeps a totem park.

moments.title: Klawock
moments.text: Twenty-one poles, original and replica, stand in the totem park, brought from the old village of Tuxekan, and in 1878 the first cannery in Alaska opened here.

moments.title: Kasaan
moments.text: The village moved in the early 1900s to be nearer a copper mine, and in 1938 its totem poles followed, to stand now with Chief Son-I-Hat's Whale House.

practical: Use four-wheel drive or a sturdy SUV for the logging roads. Fuel is sold in Craig, Klawock, Naukati, Thorne Bay, Coffman Cove and Whale Pass.
